The Pugalur channel is a contour channel off takes on the right bank of River Cauvery on the upstream side of Jeddarpalayam Bed Regulator (JBR) and runs for a length of 33.60 km. It has two branches viz. Popular Mudhaliyar channel and Pugalur Low level channel (Pallavaikkal). The Pugalur channel runs idle for about 14.40km from head works at JBR. In this portion, it runs parallel and closer to River Cauvery. In this extent, it functions as a flood carrier, carrying a part of Cauvery flood water during floods. The common bund between River Cauvery and Pugalur channel in this portion gets affected during heavy flood in Cauvery. The Pugalur channel bund has also been eroded and weakened in many places.

CHENNAI - STATE INFORMATION CENTRE

The State Information centre is functioning under the Information and Public Relations Department in the premises of Kalaivanar Arangam, Chennai. It houses a library which functions on all working days from 9.45 am to 5.45 pm. The library has about 67,000 books in Tamil and English on various subjects including Tamil Literature, Science, Research articles, Law, Medicine, Psychology, Spiritual, Astrology, Physical Education, Yoga, History, Politics, Culture, Education, Biographies of Leaders, Novels, Short Stories and Poems. These books are available to the Public, Scientists, Artists, Students and Professors for reference and study in a calm and pleasant environment.

Tamil and English Newspapers and periodical magazines are also kept in this library for reading. Notes and Publications of Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and Other Government Publications are compiled and maintained for reference.

The School and College students visit this library to take notes for their education and to take part in various literary competitions such as oratorical competitions, essay writing, poetry recitals and quizzes. The library is also equipped with books for competitive examinations.

The daily newspapers, weekly and monthly periodicals of more than two years are preserved here for the use of various departments of the Government and research scholars.

This State Information Centre Library receives two copies of the books published by various publishers for the purpose of copyright registration and the copyright information contained in the books only is being duly recorded and maintained here.

There are about 67000 books in this library and for easy reference and search, about 63,000 books have been entered into the system with the required software at a cost of Rupees Three Lakh and Sixty Thousand.

TAMILARASU

The former Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Muthamizh Arignar Dr.Kalaignar amalgamated various magazines brought out by different Departments of Government of Tamil Nadu into one Government magazine “Tamilarasu” and published it monthly on July 1, 1970.

Tamilarasu magazine was being printed from several private presses. Hence, a printing press exclusively for printing Tamilarasu magazine was formed in 1972 by Muthamizh Arignar Dr.Kalaignar. Tamilarasu press which was functioning from its building in the Omanthurar Government Estate is now functioning from Taramani, Chennai.

Tamilarasu has completed the golden jubilee year and continues its service with excellence. At present, Tamilarasu magazine is published as a monthly edition both in Tamil and English. As it compiles and publishes all the welfare schemes and achievements of the Government in a magazine format, it can be considered as a print media.

5.1.8 Relief to the families of deceased / injured fishermen due to shooting incidents by Sri Lankan Navy and others

The fishermen of coastal Districts, who fish

in their traditional waters of the Palk Bay are

apprehended / harassed and sometimes even

shot at by the Sri Lankan Navy.

The Government is providing an ex-gratia

payment of Rs.3 lakh from the Chief Minister’s

Public Relief Fund to help the family of fishermen

who die as a result of shooting at sea. In the case

of the deceased fisherman being the sole

breadwinner of the family, an ex-gratia amount of

Rs.5 lakh is provided. If the fishermen sustain

major and minor injuries, an ex-gratia amount of

Rs.50,000/- and Rs.20,000/- is provided

respectively.

higher education of children of the missing/

deceased fishermen due to Sri Lankan Naval

attack, a corpus fund of Rs.25 lakh has been

created in Tamil Nadu Fishermen Welfare Board.
